title: Stabilize TOML diagnostics across the declared supported Bun runtime range
summary: Stabilize TOML diagnostics across the declared supported Bun runtime range
description:
Reported from the cli-test review and Orbitfall project exercise on 2026-09-04. Installed tools: Lore 0.4.1 and Quest 0.3.2, macOS ARM64. Source review revisions: Lore 054e6590f1b81fda418c9891611f84fd35aacf6e; Quest dcb06f6520e08f2755c04166cca168318a94ae5a. Findings describe those tested versions, not a claim that current HEAD was retested. Evidence paths below are retained in the sibling cli-test checkout; the reproduction and outcomes are also included here. Filing is not a fix.

Source/runtime compatibility finding, distinct from the installed native binary: package engines advertises bun >=1.3.14, with packageManager pinned to 1.3.14. In disposable clones of the recorded Lore revision, run bun test test/config.test.ts with Bun 1.3.14 and Bun 1.4.0.
Observed: all 47 configuration tests pass on 1.3.14; five fail on 1.4.0. Full suites: pinned 2809 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; 1.4.0 2804 pass / 1 skip / 5 fail. The failures concern malformed TOML reason classes, parser submessages and unsafe integer hints/signs, including parent_page_id = 9007199254740993 under [confluence]. src/config.ts relies on native Bun.TOML.parse diagnostic wording.
Expected: actionable stable Lore diagnostics across the supported range, or an accurately constrained/documented runtime support contract. This is not evidence that the compiled installed binary fails on those inputs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Malformed TOML and unsafe positive/negative integer diagnostics expose stable actionable Lore errors on every advertised supported runtime.
The five failing configuration contracts pass, or intentionally revised contracts and support bounds are documented with justification.
CI covers the pinned runtime and the newest supported runtime so parser wording changes are detected.
